COVID VIRTUAL GAME DRIVES

By: Siniketiwe Hlanze | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Whilst we won't be able to enjoy the outdoors for some times, virtual game allow you experience wild life in the comfort of your home.

Unique Selling Point:
Nature lovers and those who want a break from quarantine are streaming virtual game drives from the Kruger National Park to destress. Wild Earth TV has been around for a number of years but has seen an increase in audience numbers as many people around the world are under lockdown, there's been a particular spike in the online viewers from South Africa.

Summary:
Wild Earth has rangers that go for game drives at the Kruger National Park twice a day, these are streamed live and they have a camera overlooking a waterwhole at the Djuma Game Reserve which runs on their youtube channel on a daily basis. The game drive allows people to ask questions, the ranger answers these as he drives around the park. Viewers can watch these at no costs, children's participation is encouraged as during the morning game drive only children are allowed to ask questions. The founding premise of Wild Earth Tv is to expose people wo nature and the wild an added benefit to these game drives is the psychological effects it has on people who are battling anxiety and other mental health issues at this time.

Further information:
Interview with founder - Graham Wallington in Johannesburg. Footage of game drives and waterwhole feed will be provided by Wild Earth TV

Press Release:


Virtual Game Drives
It used to be that you had to physically go to a wildlife park for a leisurely early-morning game drive. Now COVID-19 is forcing organisers to think out of the box. From lions to elephants and springboks, game rangers are taking tourists and park visitors to the animals, right in the comfort of their own homes. Carte Blanche takes a virtual drive through the wild side of the global pandemic.
Producer: Siniketiwe Hlanze | Presenter: Derek Watts


Script:



VO: UPSOUND VISUALS
Renowned for its majestic wild life South Africa is undoubtedly a beautiful country.
But due to COVID-19 nature reserves remain closed to both local and international visitors for the foreseeable future.




Graham 08:27“we’re simulating the experience of going on safari, so we’re trying to give our viewers at home the experience of going on a game drive
General nature/wild life
Wild Earth Tv – is a free online daily safari...




Graham Wellington is the CEO and Co-founder of WildEarthTV - operating from the Masai Mara in Kenya, parts of KwaZulu Natal and the Kruger National Park.

05:20 Graham “our viewers often speak about they find themselves watching the game drive in the morning and three hours later it feels like just a few minutes and they’ve just disappeared into this world”



00:20 SO the inspiration behind wild earth is that everybody wants to connect with nature and it’s a difficult thing to do and we’ve dedicated our lives to trying to figure out how best to share nature with anybody no matter where in the world they are.


01:33 But most importantly are the kids, because obviously kids are our future, and what we do now is to find a way for kids to fall in love with wild life.


Because of its appeal to kids, Wild Earth Tv has been incorporated into some hospitals in the United States to aid in the recovery and wellness of ill children


02:43 Graham “some years ago what happened was a hospital in ohio, in the un pediatrics oncology ward started to show kids that were going through chemo therapy our live safari experiences and they noticed an amazing thing, they noticed the kids were distracted, they felt less pain, they were able to suffer through their treatment more effectively and we were amazed by this and ehm we began a partnership through the children’s hospital in Washington DC where we regularly send our live feeds into the hospital, kids have a screen and they can phone down through to the Ryan Seacrest foundation Studio which are then sent through to us here in Africa and we answer them by name and we found this to be a powerful way to provide healing to people who are stuck hospitals and can’t access the outside. External hospital shots



To make these daily virtual game drives happen, it takes

Three teams, made of a ranger and a camera operator on a safari van. Then a crew in a control room, who cuts between cameras, to bring the viewer rolling coverage of the wild on Youtube
Graham 00:46 So the minute the world went into locked down we saw a massive increase in our viewership and obviously that’s because more and more people are at home and they are looking for a way to connect with nature but here in south Africa a wats app message went viral and we’ve seen a fifteen fold growth in our South African traffic and a five fold growth in our growth overall

Behind the scenes, shots of cameramen on van, cameraman focusing camera, control room visuals

Long time followers of the channel, begin to form virtual bonds with some of the animals. Like Hosana, a leopard that was orphaned at a young age
















11:30 Graham “this was really really difficult for him, he struggled to feed himself he was forced to live on the odd terrapin which is the little turtle that he would kill and it was very tough times when he lost his mom, he then lost his mom Shongile and he was on his own. And he didn’t leave he just stayed with us and he became a firm favourite he would live in the waterwhole where there’s a small camera that we have, and our viewers around the clock would watch him there. And I think all of us just began to feel like we were his mother, and now he’s left and everybody there’s facebook groups that track him, he’ll show up somewhere, and he’s like the scarlet pimpernel of the leopard world.
*Djuma Waterwhole Girrafes
0:23


Over years, these moments in the wild have been a chance for people to escape the pressures of life and Wellington believes Wild Earth TV has become a way to cope with the uncertain times of a global pandamic.
